verdict.rationale: YubiKey's own documentation says FIDO2 operations require a physical touch (user presence), with optional PIN verification. For example, the SSH keys it guards need a touch for each cryptographic operation, and community users confirm that touch-to-sign cannot be triggered remotely. Using this as an approval gate for agent-initiated actions, though, depends on routing those actions through touch-gated operations like SSH or signing, or on custom SDK integration. Missing for 10: documented agent or automation approval workflows, guidance for gating arbitrary sensitive actions (beyond SSH and signing) on a touch, and independent hands-on corroboration in AI-agent contexts.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can require a physical key touch as the human-approval step for sensitive automated or agent-initiated actions

citations.quote: FIDO2 also requires user presence (a touch on your YubiKey) for cryptographic operations, and can optionally enforce user verification (PIN entry).
The whole point of this touch to sign is that it can't be hacked remotely
